script.text: My teacher knew what time my bedroom light went off. I hadn't told him. I hadn't told anyone.
I was 15.
He'd ask who I walked home with, whether my mom worked late,
One day he asked why I'd stop taking the main road home.
Then I realized I hadn't mentioned changing my route.
I told my friend,
She walked home with me the next day. We stopped at a stationery shop. Across the street beside a parked car was my teacher.
Then a message came from a number I didn't recognize. Did you get home safely? It was him.
I typed yes, sir. Thank you. I hate remembering that. I was scared, and I still added thank you.
The messages got stranger.
don't mention these chats at school. People misunderstand kindness.
I didn't reply to that one. The next morning, he put my notebook on my desk, leaned down, and said, Ignoring people isn't very nice.
That evening, I left my lamp on while I went downstairs. When I came back, there was another message. Long night studying?
My bedroom faced the lane. From the road, you couldn't see me, just the light behind the curtain. And suddenly, all those questions sounded different.
I took the phone to my mom. I tried to start with the first message, but I couldn't get the words out, so I just handed it over.
She read it twice, then she shut the curtain.
The next morning, she came to school with me. We took screenshots. My friend told them about the shop.
He called it concern, said I'd taken it the wrong way. Mom asked why concern needed to be a secret. He didn't answer that.
He said it when mom was standing right there. I was only checking you were getting enough sleep.
I was moved to another class while the school dealt with it.
The messages stopped.
He sounded so reasonable. That's the part that still bothers me. He said it like we'd misunderstood him. Like watching my window was the most normal thing in the world.
